intent: A size you can feel: a compare chart puts the bird beside a sparrow and a pigeon so it looks like a mistake, then the bird's own swamp rises out of the island with the bird sticker on it while a wing-beat sticker shivers, and the coffee-bean egg card closes on a pin in the swamp.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country is home to the SMALLEST bird?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which country is home to the smallest bird?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Cuba. The bee hummingbird, about 6 centimetres long and lighter than a coin.

lines.direction: ease back so the whole island sits in frame; the size compare rises on 'Brazil' with the bird a sliver beside a sparrow and a pigeon; the Brazilian flag-ball thinks on 'Brazil', the Costa Rican one on 'Costa'; the island pulses on 'island'
lines.text: Brazil and Costa Rica are hummingbird country. The smallest of all lives only on this island.

lines.direction: tighten on the south-west of the island; the swamp outline lights and rises with the bird sticker on it on 'wings'; a wind sticker shivers on 'second'; a flower sticker on 'flowers' as the island pulses; the swamp settles at the end
lines.text: Its wings beat around 80 times a second, and it visits up to 1,500 flowers a day.

lines.direction: ease back a little; the COFFEE BEAN card and an egg sticker on 'egg'; the stronghold pin lands on 'nest' with a nest sticker; the Cuban flag-ball grins on 'thimble' as the island pulses; the pin leaves at the end
lines.text: The egg is the size of a coffee bean, laid in a nest no bigger than a thimble.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Lighter than a coin. Follow us.
